pages.text: A cooling tower in $(l)three sizes$(). Uranium $(l)Fuel Rods$() heat its core, $(l)water$() carries the heat away and leaves as $(l)Steam$() for $(l:nuclear/steam_turbine)Steam Turbines$(/l). The scene shows the Small tower; a $(l:basics/multiblock_projector)Multiblock Projector$(/l) shows any size right where you want to build it.

Bigger towers burn more rods, reach more power and move more heat; small ones are cheap but limited:$(br)$(li)$(l)Small$(): 5x5 x 7, 2, 200%, 150 / 375 / 900 per tick$(br)$(li)$(l)Medium$(): 7x7 x 11, 4, 350%, 250 / 625 / 1,500 per tick$(br)$(li)$(l)Large$(): 9x9 x 15, 8, 500%, 400 / 1,000 / 2,400 per tick
pages.title: Building the tower

pages.text: Every tower is a full square floor, then hollow square rings, wide at the bottom and the rim and narrow at the waist. Layer by layer from the bottom (ring width in blocks):$(br)$(li)$(l)Small$(): 5x5, 5, 5, 3, 3, 3, 5$(br)$(li)$(l)Medium$(): 7x7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 5, 5, 5, 5, 5, 7, 7$(br)$(li)$(l)Large$(): 9x9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 9, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 7, 9, 9, 9

Blocks outside a narrower ring do not matter; everything inside the rings must be empty.$(br)$(li)Use $(item)Reactor Casing$()s for the shell.$(br)$(li)Put the $(item)Fission Reactor Controller$() $(l)in the middle of one side of layer 2$(), facing out. The controller finds the size by itself, trying the largest first.

$(li)Swap any shell blocks for $(item)Reactor Port$()s where you want to connect pipes, cables or hoppers. Two are enough: one for water in, one for steam out.$(br)$(li)The inside must be $(l)empty$().

$(li)A Large tower makes more steam than a basic $(l:cables/gas_pipe)Gas Pipe$(/l) carries (1,000 mB/t): use $(l)Advanced$() pipes at its steam port.$(br)When the tower is complete it powers up with a deep chime and $(l)turns into a real cooling tower$(): the blocky casings disappear into one smooth, curved shell of white panels with

glowing pale green bands, wide at the base, narrow in the middle and flared at the rim. The controller becomes a $(l)panel$() on the surface and every port a glowing $(l)hatch$(), right where a pipe or cable plugged into the port enters the tower. You can $(l)right-click any block of the tower$() to open the reactor.
$(li)$(l)Left$(): the water tank and the $(l)coolant$() tank (see below).$(br)$(li)$(l)Title$(): the size of the tower.
pages.title: The reactor GUI

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Middle$(): 8 Fuel Rod slots (the ones a smaller tower cannot burn are dimmed), the core (one bar per rod, emerald while it burns) and 4 waste slots for Depleted Fuel Rods. Below them, the $(l)temperature$() bar with the red alarm mark.

$(li)$(l)Bottom$(): the $(l)power$() controls, from $(o)Off$() up to the tower's maximum, in steps of 50%.$(br)$(li)$(l)Right$(): the steam tank.$(br)A new reactor starts $(l)Off$(): insert rods, connect water, then raise the power.

Reactor Ports are where the outside world connects:$(br)$(li)$(l)Fuel Rods (hoppers, pipes of other mods)$(): Depleted Fuel Rods$(br)$(li)Water and coolant ($(l:cables/liquid_pipe)Liquid Pipes$(/l)): Steam, pushed out by itself ($(l:cables/gas_pipe)Gas Pipes$(/l))
pages.title: Ports

pages.text: Each rod makes $(l)50 heat per tick at 100% power$(): 4 rods at 250% make 500. The heat goes into the $(l)water$(), 1 mB of water for each unit of heat, and leaves as the same amount of $(l)Steam$(): more power, more steam, more FE.$(br2)How much heat can leave each tick depends on the tower
pages.title: Power, heat and cooling

pages.text: size (table above) and on the $(l)primary loop$() in the coolant tank: plain water moves the base amount, $(l:nuclear/coolant_mixer)Coolant$(/l) $(l)2.5 times$() as much and $(l:nuclear/coolant_mixer)Cryo Coolant$(/l) $(l)6 times$(). A Large tower at full power (8 rods at 500% = 2,000 heat) needs Cryo Coolant; a Small one at 200% (200 heat) only needs Coolant.

Coolants wear out slowly while they work (1 mB per 400 heat moved). Water and steam room are needed too: without water, or with the steam tank full because the turbines cannot keep up, the heat has nowhere to go.

Heat that cannot leave stays in the core and the $(l)temperature$() rises (hover the bar for the details).$(br)$(li)Above $(l)80%$() an $(l)alarm$() rings and the GUI flashes $(o)OVERHEATING$(). Turn the power down, add water or coolant, or make room for the steam.
pages.title: Overheating and meltdown

pages.text: $(li)At $(l)100%$() the core $(l)melts down$(): the rods are destroyed, the tower $(l)explodes$() and the area around it becomes heavily $(l:nuclear/radiation)radioactive$(/l) for a long time.$(br)An idle core cools down slowly by itself.
$(l)No escape$(): breaking a block of the tower, or the controller, while the temperature is above 80% does not save you. The core melts down anyway. Turn the power to Off and let it cool first.
